title: Post-Appeal Applications in Capital Cases Bill
what_it_is: Post-Appeal Applications in Capital Cases Bill

sections.label: Post-appeal applications in capital cases
sections.summary: The measures provide a process for post-appeal applications filed by prisoners awaiting capital punishment after all appeals are exhausted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: What we are putting forward before you today are measures to provide a process for post-appeal applications in capital cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Post-appeal applications in capital cases are applications that are filed by a prisoner awaiting capital punishment, or PACP, after all avenues of appeal have been exhausted.

sections.label: Clause 2 PACC procedure
sections.summary: Clause 2 introduces a new procedure in the Supreme Court of Judicature Act 1969 for post-appeal applications in capital cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 2 introduces a new procedure in the Supreme Court of Judicature Act 1969, or SCJA, for post-appeal applications in capital cases, or PACC applications.

sections.label: CA permission required
sections.summary: A prisoner awaiting capital punishment must obtain the Court of Appeal's permission before filing a PACC application.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: A PACP must obtain the CA’s permission before he may file a PACC application.

sections.label: Pending applications bar subsequent filings
sections.summary: A prisoner cannot make a subsequent PACC permission application or PACC application while one is pending, unless the coram dealing with it grants permission.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: If there is already an application for PACC permission, or a PACC application, pending determination, the PACP cannot make a subsequent application for PACC permission or PACC application unless the PACP has obtained the permission of the coram dealing with the pending application.

sections.label: Stay and abuse of process
sections.summary: New sections 60L and 60M provide that only the Court of Appeal may grant a stay of execution and may find an abuse of process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In line with the procedure for PACC applications, which must be made to the CA, the new section 60L of the SCJA provides that a stay of execution of a capital sentence may only be granted by the CA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The new section 60M of the SCJA provides that the CA may decide whether to make a finding that there has been an abuse of process in (a) a relevant application or (b) any other application or action in order to delay or frustrate the carrying out of the capital sentence.

sections.label: When capital sentence may be carried out
sections.summary: Clause 3(a) provides a capital sentence may be carried out unless there is a respite, a stay, or a pending qualifying application.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 3(a) also provides that a capital sentence may be carried out, unless (a) the President has ordered a respite; (b) the CA has granted a stay of execution; or (c) there is a pending application for permission to apply for a stay of execution, or an application for a stay of execution, that meets the specified criteria.

sections.label: Workers' Party vote against Bill
sections.summary: The Workers' Party would vote against the Bill if it closed off new evidence or arguments in post-appeal applications in capital cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If this Bill was meant to close off the possibility of new evidence being heard or new legal arguments being made in post-appeal applications in capital cases, or PACCs, the Workers' Party would vote against this Bill.

sections.label: Court of Appeal new evidence power
sections.summary: The Bill empowers the Court of Appeal to take new evidence and regulates the process without closing off defences not heard at trial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Court of Appeal is to be empowered under the Bill to take new evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While this Bill may appear to some as putting a spanner in the works for lawyers who wish to file PACCs, in my view, it serves to regulate the process better and does not close off defences not heard at trial.

sections.label: Reasonable prospect for success
sections.summary: Section 60G(7)(d) requires consideration of whether the PACC application has a reasonable prospect for success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In particular, the matter for consideration in section 60G(7)(d) is whether the PACC application has a reasonable prospect for success.

sections.label: No discretion for abuse of process
sections.summary: Proposed section 60G(15) provides that where there has been abuse of process, the Court of Appeal must not grant PACC permission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The proposed section 60G(15) provides that where there has been abuse of process, the Court of Appeal, I quote, "must not" grant the application for PACC permission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The phrase used is "must not", which can only mean that the Court of Appeal judge has no discretion in the matter.

sections.label: Must not grant PACC permission
sections.summary: Under section 60G(15)(d), the Court of Appeal must not grant the application for PACC permission in such a scenario.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In such a possible scenario, based on the Bill before us, due to section 60G(15)(d), the Court of Appeal must not grant the application for PACC permission.

sections.label: Removing Court of Appeal discretion
sections.summary: The passage asks whether it is necessary to remove the Court of Appeal's discretion in this case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Is it necessary to remove the Court of Appeal's discretion in this case?

sections.label: New PACC procedures and court factors
sections.summary: New provisions clarify PACC procedures and factors the Court considers in granting permission, ensuring due process in capital cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new provisions will clarify the procedures for PACCs and the factors that the Court has to consider in granting permission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given the serious nature of capital cases, it is critical that due process is in place to ensure that meritorious applications by prisoners awaiting capital punishment are heard.

sections.label: Reasonable prospect of success
sections.summary: The Court considers whether a PACC application has a reasonable prospect of success when deciding whether to grant PACC permission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Court is required to consider whether the PACC application has a reasonable prospect of success in deciding whether or not to grant an application for PACC permission.

sections.label: Abuse of process bars permission
sections.summary: Under section 60G(15)(c), the Court of Appeal must not grant PACC permission if the applicant abused the process of court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under section 60G(15)(c), the Court of Appeal must not grant an application for PACC permission if the applicant is found to have abused the process of court.

sections.label: Free legal representation via LASCO
sections.summary: Accused persons charged with capital offences in Singapore are typically offered free legal representation through LASCO, regardless of nationality and means.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu had shared earlier, in Singapore, an accused person being charged with a capital offence will typically be offered free legal representation at trial and/or appeal through the Supreme Court's Legal Assistance Scheme for Capital Offences, in short LASCO, regardless of his or her nationality and means.

sections.label: Personal costs futile for PACPs
sections.summary: Ordering personal costs may be futile as PACPs often have limited means, so the Bill introduces new procedures with enhanced safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Ordering of personal costs, as one Member has suggested earlier, may be futile as PACPs more often than not, are of limited means.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I therefore support this Bill, which seeks to deal with post-appeal applications in a capital case with a prisoner awaiting capital punishment, by introducing new procedures with enhanced safeguards for post-appeal applications.

sections.label: LASCO extension to PACC applications
sections.summary: The question asks whether LASCO would be extended to cover PACC permission and PACC applications occurring after clemency was sought and rejected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this instance, would the LASCO scheme be extended to cover applications for PACC permission and PACC which may have occurred at a much later date after Presidential clemency has already been sought but rejected?

sections.label: Court of Appeal judges assignment
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarification on when one, three or five Court of Appeal judges hear permission and PACC applications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this aspect, I wish to seek the Senior Parliamentary Secretary's clarification: under what circumstances would one, three or even five Court of Appeal judges be assigned to hear application for permission to make PACC application as well as PACC application?

sections.label: Post-appeal applications in capital cases
sections.summary: The Bill balances due process and PACC rights against preventing undue waste from frivolous PACC applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is thus not unsurprising that in capital offence cases, there is not only a thorough trial and appellate process where the Courts are careful and meticulous in sifting through the evidence and arguments, but there is also comprehensive support such as pro bono legal assistance through LASCO.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, recently there have been many post-appeal applications in capital cases, also known as PACCs, which take up many years and judicial resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Some of these PACCs were still being filed seven to 13 years after the first conviction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These PACCs take up not only judicial time and resources but in actual fact they have robbed the convicted inmates, and most importantly, their families, of what is left in their lifetime, and victims' families of a time for closure and peace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill ensures that in respect of PACC applications, there is a balance between due process and rights of PACP and also preventing the resources of the state from being unduly wasted by frivolous PACC applications.

sections.label: Single judge PACC hearing
sections.summary: The new process for a single judge hearing a PACC will save significant judicial time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The new process for a single judge hearing a PACC will save a significant amount of judicial time.

sections.label: Death penalty under international law
sections.summary: International law does not prohibit the death penalty, and Singapore applies capital punishment only to the most serious crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under International law, the death penalty is not prohibited, whether by the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) or any other international treaty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, capital punishment is only applied to the most serious crimes that cause grave harm to others and to society.

sections.label: PACC Bill consistency with standards
sections.summary: The PACC Bill clarifying due process beyond appeal is consistent with international law standards and safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In my view, this PACC Bill which further clarifies the due process beyond the appellate process is consistent with not only international law standards but also the safeguards aforesaid.

sections.label: Support for PACC Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill and clarifies that it merely provides the Court must consider matters in section 60G(7).

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the clarifications, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I stand in support of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: With regards to the first clarification that he raised, what was meant is that the Bill merely provides that the Court must consider the matters in section, 60G(7).

sections.label: Court's power to take evidence
sections.summary: The Court may take additional evidence on its own motion or on a party's application.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The Court's power to take additional evidence is exercisable on the Court's own motion, or upon a party's application.

sections.label: PACC permission after abuse finding
sections.summary: The CA may grant PACC permission despite a prior abuse of process finding if new material is adduced that could not have been adduced earlier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Under the new sections 60G(15)(c) and (d) of the SCJA, even when there was a prior abuse of process finding, as I mentioned earlier, the CA may grant an application for PACC permission if: one, the PACP adduces material that was not adduced in court before the date of the most recent finding of abuse of process; and two, the material could not, even with reasonable diligence, have been adduced in court before that date.

sections.label: Incidental directions and interim orders
sections.summary: The Bill allows the Court to make incidental directions or interim orders, including a stay of execution, and requires the CA to consider written submissions before summary refusal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: In line with Mr Zhulkarnain's suggestions, the Bill expressly allows the Court to make any incidental directions or give any interim orders as considered necessary for the management of the case, including a stay of execution of the capital sentence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: For example, when a criminal motion was filed on 25 April 2022, two days before the PACP's scheduled execution, the Court heard the matter the very next day, on 26 April 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The Bill requires the CA to consider the applicant's written submissions, if any, before summarily refusing an application.
